_doc: PPC Command Brief — grading formula and receiving-model constraints. Single source of truth for the weights; src/amazon_ads/brief_score.py is the only implementation. Changing a weight here changes the CLI, the dashboard and the tests together. Bump formula_version whenever a weight or breakpoint changes so week-over-week scores are never silently compared across formulas.

acos_vs_breakeven.label: ACOS vs break-even
acos_vs_breakeven._doc: acos / break_even_acos. At or under 0.70 of break-even is full marks; at 1.5x break-even every incremental sale loses money at scale.

tacos_vs_band.label: TACoS vs target band
tacos_vs_band._doc: Inside the band is full marks. Below the band is NOT a failure but is not full marks either — it usually means under-investment rather than efficiency. Above the band decays linearly to zero.

wasted_spend.label: Wasted spend share
wasted_spend._doc: Share of ad spend on search terms with zero attributed orders in the window. Rolled up per term, never per term-day.

placement_health.label: Placement health
placement_health._doc: Worst placement ACOS divided by account ACOS, over placements clearing the spend floor. A placement with spend and no sales is treated as no_sales_ratio rather than being skipped.

brand_defense.label: Brand defense (not overspending on our own name)
brand_defense._doc: Brand terms are defended, not scaled. Scores the share of ad spend going to branded queries against a ceiling; zero credit at zero_credit_multiple x ceiling.

non_brand_efficiency.label: Non-brand efficiency where rank allows
non_brand_efficiency._doc: ACOS vs break-even restricted to non-brand terms whose organic rank band is eligible_rank_min or worse — i.e. where paid traffic is additive rather than cannibalising our own organic placement. Terms with unknown rank are excluded, not assumed.

completeness_modifier._doc: A small multiplier, never a component. Thin data should temper confidence in the score without inventing a performance result. Applied last: final = weighted x multiplier.

rank_coverage._doc: Share of non-brand terms carrying an organic rank band.

sqp_freshness._doc: Days between the newest stored SQP week_end and the brief's as-of date. Amazon publishes SQP a week in arrears, so 14 days is current.

ads_freshness._doc: Days since the last successful ads sync.

letters.reading: Efficient and defended. Spend into what is working.
Healthy with a specific leak. Fix the P0 list and re-grade.
Break-even-ish. Waste is funding itself; cut before scaling.
Losing money on a meaningful share of spend. Stop the bleeding first.
Spend is not paying for itself. Cut placements and negatives before any raise.

action_plan._doc: P0 first. Rank-blocked raises are never emitted as 'raise bid' — they appear in the held list instead.

receiving_model_rules: Use ONLY this brief. Every number you cite must appear in it verbatim. If something is not here, say "insufficient evidence" — do not estimate, benchmark, or reason from general Amazon knowledge.
Prefer the P0/P1 actions already listed. Do not invent campaigns, ad groups, search terms, or bid values that do not appear in this brief.
Brand terms are a defend line, never a growth lever. Bids that this brief marks rank-capped, rank-unknown or held stay held — do not recommend raising them.
Distinguish observation from proof. Before/after windows around a change are observational; say so, and never describe a correlation as a cause.
If a section says "No data", that is a finding to report, not a gap to fill with an assumption.
required_output_sections: B. Do this week — ordered checklist
